findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'extend tools/sweep-selftests.py's watched set to the checkout's own .claude/ so a write there is a finding naming the suite': CLAUDE_UNWATCHED removes state, logs, usage, worktrees, settings.local.json and audit-panel.json from the watched set, and those are most of the places the plugin writes under .claude/ (the checkout's .gitignore already lists state/, usage/ and logs/). The executor's own known offender, tests/test_audit_task.py writing .claude/state/{.gitignore,bash-writes-plugin-cli.json,writer-token.json} when TMPDIR sits in a clone, passes this guard unseen. A suite that exercises the usage ledger, a hook log or worktree creation against its own location would be invisible the same way. The exemption is by subtree name, so it hides every suite write there along with the live session's.
findings.resolution: Narrow the exemption from a subtree to what the live session really writes. Options: (a) for state/logs/usage, watch the NAMES a suite is known to leak (writer-token.json, bash-writes-plugin-cli.json, state/.gitignore) with a case per name; (b) have sweep() refuse or loudly report when the scratch root (TMPDIR) is under the watched checkout, since that is the precondition for the unwatched leak (this overlaps P137.4, so the task may only file the cheap loud line); (c) at least add a case pinning which known suite-writes are NOT caught, so the blind spot is a recorded fact and not only a comment.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'a write there is a finding naming the suite': a write attributed to a suite is passed to grade() as debris, but grade() returns 'exited N' (or the raw timeout text) before it reads debris. A suite that writes into .claude/ and also exits non-zero or times out therefore gets no finding, and the write is not put in the loose row either, so it is lost. This is the very case the task reproduces: with TMPDIR in a clone, test_migrate_manifest.py writes audit-backups/ and then dies with FileNotFoundError, so the sweep shows only 'exited 1' and never names the write. The executor notes this as a limit, but the diff leaves it in place.
findings.resolution: In sweep(), when the graded row is not ok and by_suite holds lines for it, append claude_debris(...) to the row's why. Or move those lines into `loose` so claude_row reports them. Add a case with a suite that writes into .claude/ and then exits 1.

findings.issue: The 'never blame a clean suite' rule (comment at 144-153) does not hold for deletions and for added directories. A DELETED entry is timed by the nearest surviving ancestor's mtime in the AFTER snapshot, and an ADDED directory by its own mtime. A directory's mtime moves with any later entry change directly under it, including entries the guard does not watch (state/ appearing, settings.local.json rewritten by rename, __pycache__). Example: suite A deletes .claude/keep at t1, and the live session or suite B then touches a direct child of .claude/ at t2. The deletion is stamped t2 and pinned on whichever single suite holds t2, which may be a clean one. cw6 asserts the stamps against fixed numbers (99, 66) and cannot see this.
findings.resolution: Do not time a deletion (or an added directory) from a directory stamp that other changes can move. Give it at=None and report it in the loose row naming every suite whose window overlaps the whole sweep, with its own wording. The current loose text for at=None says 'no suite's run holds the moment', which is untrue of a deletion that has no moment.

findings.issue: The 20 ms start slack is applied to every window, so at --jobs 1 two adjacent suites' windows overlap by up to the slack whenever the gap between one ended_ns and the next began_ns is shorter than it. A write in the last milliseconds of a suite then has two candidates, and the printed advice ('Re-run ... with --jobs 1 to name the one that wrote') can loop back to 'unattributed'. cw0 passes only because the writer sleeps 0.4 s after writing. The comment says windows 'cannot overlap' at --jobs 1.
findings.resolution: Resolve ties on the raw windows first: if exactly one raw (unslacked) window holds the moment, name it; use the slack only when no raw window does. Add a case with a write at ended_ns - 1 ms and a neighbour starting 5 ms later.

intent.note: Matches on two clauses. 'Find the suite ... make it use a scratch project': the executor found tests/test_migrate_manifest.py (not a REPO_ROOT use; the cause is TMPDIR inside a clone, since _manifest_io.checkout_of walks up to the clone's .git) and added _outside_any_checkout, which allocates the two in-place-migration fixture roots outside any checkout and fails loudly if none exists. The red-first on the description's own terms (cw0 fails on the unfixed sweep) is claimed. Diverges on the third clause, 'extend tools/sweep-selftests.py's watched set to the checkout's own .claude/ so a write there is a finding naming the suite'. The diff watches the directory minus CLAUDE_UNWATCHED (state, logs, usage, worktrees, settings.local.json, audit-panel.json, __pycache__), so a write under those is not a finding (finding 1). It also drops the suite's name when the writer exits non-zero or times out (finding 2). Whether the executor's outcome describes the diff: yes, and it discloses the blind spot and the exited-N loss honestly. Two statements are stronger than the code. 'never one suite picked at random' does not hold for deletions and added directories (finding 3). '--jobs 1 names the writer' is not guaranteed with the slack (finding 4). The outcome's dependants answer holds: run_one gained two keys, sweep() gains at most one row, and no flag, output line or exit code changes in a green run. The tests/ dependant is only test_migrate_manifest.py, additive. Judgements asked for. (a) Attribution by mtime against wall-clock windows: with exactly one window holding the moment the suite is named. With two or more it files one red unattributed row listing every candidate, and cw3 drives that with real overlapping children. Overlap is handled honestly. The weaknesses are the directory-stamp cases (finding 3) and the slack (finding 4). (b) CLAUDE_UNWATCHED does hide channels a suite can really write through: state, logs, usage and worktrees are all plugin write targets, and test_audit_task.py is a real instance. Would this guard catch the P137.4 root cause, TMPDIR inside the checkout? Not as a cause. The guard never looks at TMPDIR. It catches the symptoms that land in watched paths, such as audit-backups/ and .claude/.gitignore from the migration suite, and only as a named finding when that suite exits 0. The .claude/state writes by test_audit_task.py it misses entirely.
